structured.theme_or_track: Kababaihan at Kabataan: Katuwang sa Paghahabi ng Isang Matatag na Bayan
structured.what_it_does: Youth-led environmental advocacy that restores degraded lands and empowers communities through nature-based adaptation. Public write-ups describe kamagong and bamboo propagation, coastal clean-ups, and a goal of restoring about one hectare of degraded land per community site; related Subang work also covers ecosystem restoration, climate action, disaster preparedness, and sustainable agriculture.
structured.place: Cebu (CTU Barili Campus / Province of Cebu), Philippines
structured.outcome_or_award: Youth Category honoree, Philippine Resilience Awards 2025 (Climate Change Commission multistakeholder program; ceremony at Philippine Normal University during 18th Global Warming and Climate Change Consciousness Week). Separately reported as 2024 Outstanding Regional Youth Volunteer (Region VII / Central Visayas context via CTU coverage).
structured.gap: Could not fully retrieve CTU.edu.ph article bodies (HTTP failures on fetch); details from those URLs rest on search snippets and cross-reporting. No public ranked place (1st/2nd/etc.) among Youth Category winners—sources list him among five youth honorees. Exact Subang founding date, full co-founder roster, measured hectares restored, and funding model not verified in the official CCC/PIA/Inquirer pages used. No explicit Ateneo Youth CLAP / Youth CLAP program participation found. Facebook (Subang Philippines) claims founding March 20, 2023 at CTU-Barili and 200+ projects—not independently confirmed via primary institutional page.
structured.note: Strong CCC / PRA 2025 case study for PH youth climate resilience: nature-based land restoration + community empowerment, campus-rooted (CTU Barili BSABE student) with a named youth org (Subang / Subang CTU Chapter). Enorio is repeatedly identified as Founding / National Executive President of Subang Philippines. Related activities in public coverage include black bamboo propagation (2026 launch with CTU Barili), waste/agriculture initiatives, and disaster relief (e.g. Subang–CTU coordinated relief). PRA partners include CCC, PCW, National Resilience Council, SM Prime, WiNDRR, ARISE PH; awardees are promised continued support to scale. Useful angle for student teams: chapter model + NBS (bamboo/kamagong) + DRR community work rather than pure climate-tech hardware.
